29012.description:
WORKSHOP OPERATIONS MANAGER


Hargy Oil Palms Limited is seeking an experienced Workshop Operations Manager to coordinate the day-to-day operation of all four workshop areas at Bialla, West New Britain Province.


The role reports to the Head of Department – Vehicle Workshop and provides direct operational leadership to the Workshop Superintendents, ensuring jobs are prioritised, delays are addressed, and workshop standards are maintained.


Applicants should have strong workshop leadership, planning, reporting, safety, and practical problem-solving skills.


Key responsibilities include:




Plan, prioritise, allocate, monitor, and close out daily workshop jobs.


Lead Workshop Superintendents and report key issues to the Head of Department – Vehicle Workshop.


Oversee workshop sections including mechanics, trades, tyre bay, welding, auto-electrical, stores, and support functions.


Monitor breakdown response, repair turnaround, job cards, spare parts follow-up, and outstanding work.


Coordinate vehicle accident response, recovery, reporting, repairs, and corrective actions.


Support cost control, operational reporting, OPEX/CAPEX input, fleet feedback, and disposal preparation.


Ensure quality workmanship, correct diagnosis, final inspection, and reduced rework.


Maintain safe work practices, good housekeeping, tool control, and compliance with company OH&S and RSPO requirements.


Prepare accurate workshop records and reports on jobs completed, downtime, labour usage, parts usage, and recurring defects.




Applicants should have:




A recognised trade certificate or higher qualification in a relevant technical field.


At least 10 years’ relevant workshop, fleet, plant, or heavy equipment maintenance experience.


Experience coordinating workshop operations and reporting operational issues to senior management.


Strong skills in workflow control, manpower planning, quality, safety, and workshop discipline.


Good computer skills, including Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and workshop or fleet maintenance reporting systems.


A current driver’s licence.




Experience in plantation, transport, construction, remote-area workshop, or large fleet operations will be highly regarded.


This is a senior role within the Vehicle Workshop operations.


A very competitive salary along with housing, utilities, motor vehicle, schooling at the companies International School, Medical Insurance, as well as other excellent benefits are provided.

29000.description:
Empty Container Controller


Lae  |  Inland Container Depot Operations


Help keep our empty-container stock accurate and depot movements controlled. 
Express Freight Management is seeking a reliable, detail-focused Empty Container Controller to coordinate yard activity, stock records and gate movements across our Lae ICD yards. The position works with the ICD team, drivers, shipping-line representatives, data-entry staff and reach-stacker operators.


Key responsibilities




Maintain a current empty-container register by container number, shipping line, size and type, condition, status, yard location and movement history. Reconcile the register and IQS against physical stock through routine yard checks and scheduled stocktakes, and report variances promptly.


Coordinate empty-container gate-ins, gate-outs, inter-yard transfers, repositioning and evacuations using approved instructions and supporting documents. Keep IQS and manual movement records accurate and up to date.


Ensure drivers process the required DDs at the ICD2 gate office before moving or loading an empty container, regardless of its storage yard. Confirm that the movement is recorded so IQS stock remains accurate.


Control gate-out documentation: receive and check dockets or release instructions, verify the container number and visible condition against the physical unit, complete or check the EIR, and stamp or endorse documents only after required checks are complete.


Maintain a manual gate-out record when required and pass collected dockets and supporting records to the designated data-entry team at the required intervals, including hourly handover where the depot process requires it.


Identify and report irregularities between documents and the physical container, including incorrect container numbers, altered or unusual dockets, missing approvals, damage or other movement exceptions. Escalate before release when a discrepancy is unresolved.


Coordinate container location and lift requests between the ICD office, drivers and reach-stacker operators. Help locate containers for loading and provide clear container details and yard positions; do not operate lifting equipment unless separately trained and authorized.


Promote safe storage by checking that chains and straps used in container storage are available, serviceable and correctly managed. Support daily stacking spot-checks and report unsafe or incorrect stacking to the FCL Yard Coordinator or supervisor.


Coordinate weekly empty-container stocktakes and assist with FCL yard stocktakes when assigned. Record results clearly and follow up count differences with the relevant yard team.


Assist with additional sealing of SPB-cleared containers when instructed, and record seal details against the relevant container and supporting documents.


Where required and trained, confirm that Underbond containers requiring inspection or fumigation are positioned on the ground, and check physical seal numbers against Customs documents. Refer any mismatch to the supervisor; do not alter seals or release the unit without authorization.


Keep dockets, DDs, EIRs, stocktake sheets and other movement records organized and traceable. Provide accurate updates and reports to the ICD Manager or delegate.




What you will bring




Grade 12 completion. A certificate or diploma in logistics, transport, supply chain, business administration or a related field is an advantage.


Experience in a container depot, transport, logistics, gate control or inventory role is an advantage. Entry-level applicants with strong potential are encouraged to apply.


Attention to detail and confidence checking container numbers, documents, physical stock and data-entry records.


Basic computer skills, including accurate data entry and spreadsheets, with the ability to learn IQS and company procedures.


Clear communication and a cooperative approach with drivers, operators and office staff.


Honesty, reliability and a strong work ethic; able to work under pressure and outdoors in a physically active depot environment while following safety instructions.




This position is available for immediate start. If this sounds like you, please submit your application to this email: 
[email protected]


Please note, that ONLY shortlisted candidates will be contacted for interview. 


 





            

        
Apply

The Utilities Engineer is responsible for ensuring the safe, reliable, and continuous operation of utility plants through effective maintenance, ISO compliance, resource optimization, and operational excellence. The role is accountable for maximizing utility availability, minimizing downtime, improving efficiency, and achieving key performance targets to support uninterrupted production.


 


Main Duties will include: 




Lead, coach, and develop the Utilities Team, fostering a high-performance culture focused on safety, reliability, and continuous improvement.


Oversee and maintain Brewery utilities, including Boiler, Steam systems, compressed air, CO₂ recovery, Ammonia refrigeration, Power Generation, Water Treatment, and Wastewater Treatment


Perform troubleshooting, maintenance, and repair of utility equipment to minimize downtime and ensure compliance with safety and environmental regulations.


Monitor energy and water consumption, identifying opportunities for efficiency improvements and sustainability initiatives.


Ensure the safe, efficient, and uninterrupted operation of all utility systems supporting brewery production and packaging activities.


Coordinate preventive and corrective maintenance programs to maximize equipment reliability and minimize downtime.


Monitor utility consumption and performance, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and reduce operating costs.


Develop and implement energy, water, and sustainability initiatives that support the brewery's environmental objectives.


Ensure compliance with all relevant safety, environmental, engineering, and statutory requirements.


Manage utility-related projects including plant upgrades, equipment installations, process improvements, and capital investments.


Provide technical support and troubleshooting expertise to brewery operations, maintenance, and packaging teams.


Develop utility operating procedures, maintenance standards, and asset management plans.


Analyze utility performance data and prepare regular reports on operational performance, maintenance activities, reliability metrics, utility consumption, and cost management.


Manage contractor activities and ensure all work is conducted safely and in accordance with company standards.

Collaborate closely with Brewing, Packaging, Quality, and Engineering teams to ensure utilities effectively support production targets and business objectives.

29013.description:
Career Opportunities


The Ok Tedi Development Foundation (OTDF) is the legal entity that manages community development benefits from Ok Tedi Mine operations on behalf of the people of the 158 Community Mine Continuation Agreement (CMCA) villages.  OTDF is a safe, professional and innovative organisation that delivers projects to communities through a unique partnership between mining, the people and the government.  OTDF is mandated to ensure wise and sustainable use of the wealth created from mining operations for the betterment of future generations of Western Province.


 


OTDF currently has 
one (1
) vacancy and seeks to engage a dynamic, competent and qualified person to be part of the team that is delivering development outcomes for the communities of Western Province.  OTDF seeks to attract and retain professionals who are committed, hardworking, loyal, and honest and who possess good behaviour.


 


Manager – Program Services Operations


To lead and manage the operations of the Program Services Operations Department, including the development and implementation of short, medium and long-term strategies to enhance program quality, strengthen service delivery, and achieve effective development planning and sustainable outcomes for the communities of Western Province. This position reports to the Executive Manager Program Services.


 


Tasks and responsibilities include:




To ensure that CMCA and OTDF supported projects are delivered in a timely and efficient manner to the communities thereby maintaining regular communication with the local communities with regards to projects status of their projects and to address any community related issues that may arise.


To be accountable for ensuring cost effectiveness and efficiency in the operations of the Department and in the implementation of development planning initiatives to promote sustainable initiatives in the impacted communities and in accordance with the Community Mine Continuation Agreement (CMCA).


To promote and uphold CMCA & OTDF intent as part of the Operations team of Program Services, to orientate and infuse company ethics, values and principals across sections and to translate Organization aims into practical and achievable strategies, goals, and objectives.


To determine and control negative work-related environmental impacts and enforce company-wide workplace health & safety policy and regulations to ensure employees, contractors and stakeholders uphold company target of zero work-related incidents and accidents.


Maximise ongoing long- and short-term benefits to the stakeholders in the prescribed areas and minimize the impact on the environment through institutionalizing and monitoring the delivery of professional agricultural, agribusiness and livelihood projects, advisory services and training programs


Create excellent relationship with all stakeholders (internal & external) including PNG Government, the greater community and Western Province through establishing and maintain regular dialogue on all issues relating to development of the communities


Maintains close liaison with the management team to analyse, define, and recommend appropriate development strategies aligned with organisational priorities and project requirements. Prepares and presents current and long-term plans, forecasts, and progress reports to monitor performance, assess outcomes, and ensure the effective implementation of strategic objectives.


Ensure staff within the section are motivated, competent, and adequately trained by recognising and rewarding performance, providing constructive feedback on individual and team achievements, and fostering a high-performance work culture.


Monitor and manage the section’s capital and operational expenditure to ensure spending remains within approved budget allocations and financial targets through regular budget reviews and performance monitoring.


Establish and maintain effective top-down and bottom-up communication systems throughout the Department to promote information sharing, staff engagement, collaboration, accountability, and alignment with organisational objectives.




 


Experience, Knowledge, Skills and Competencies:




A University Degree (preferably Masters) in Development Studies, Project Management, Agribusiness, Sustainable Development, or a related field will be an added advantage.






A minimum of 10–15 years of supervisory and management experience in community development, sustainable development, or a related field, with demonstrated leadership capability.


Thorough understanding of Papua New Guinea’s economy, sustainable economic growth opportunities, cultural diversity, and community development challenges.


Sound knowledge and appreciation of sustainable development principles, OTDF’s mandate and strategic objectives, and the application of the Triple Bottom Line (People, Planet and Profit) business model.


A proven track record in planning, managing, and implementing community development programs and projects that deliver measurable and sustainable outcomes.


Strong understanding of cultural diversity, community dynamics, environmental sustainability, and the social and economic issues affecting development in Western Province and Papua New Guinea.


Demonstrated ability to inspire, lead, and mobilise teams to drive organisational change within an 18-month timeframe, strengthen operational performance, and promote continuous improvement.


Proven ability to develop and implement appropriate strategies and plans that leverage human capital, technical expertise, systems, and organisational resources to optimise performance during periods of significant change.


Excellent strategic communication and leadership skills, with the ability to articulate organisational priorities, translate strategic intent into practical action, and lead by example in fostering teamwork and accountability.


Demonstrated capacity to anticipate, manage, and lead organisational change over a 5–10-year strategic horizon, overcome resistance to change, and establish the foundations for long-term organisational success.


Strong leadership and decision-making capabilities, including the willingness to make difficult but necessary organisational decisions, manage performance issues, and contribute constructively to senior management and departmental decision-making processes.


A collaborative leadership approach, with the ability to break down organisational silos, strengthen cross-functional cooperation, and promote a unified, results-oriented team culture.


Exceptional perseverance, resilience, and commitment to seeing complex, large-scale change initiatives through to successful implementation.


Strong strategic management and execution capabilities, with a demonstrated commitment to achieving results, developing staff capabilities, mentoring emerging leaders, and preparing suitable successors to ensure leadership continuity.


A forward-thinking and entrepreneurial mindset, with the vision and drive to create significant and lasting value for OTDF, its stakeholders, and the broader community development sector in Papua New Guinea.

29070.description:
Goodman Fielder Papua New Guinea is one of PNG’s largest food companies, manufacturing and distributing high-quality Flour, Stock Feed, Snacks and Bakery products throughout the country. The company owns a host of iconic brands which include; Flame Flour, Flame Stockfeed, Bilas Bread, Arthur's Pie, Twisties, Skel Rice and the Meadow Lea range.


At GFI, we care about making everyday food better for everyone.


Our goal is to be the leading and most innovative food company with a mission to meet our customers’ needs for superior quality foods with brands that are trusted by families everywhere.  We are the go-to source of consumer, shopper, and customer insights to help our customer and business partners succeed.




Goodman Fielder PNG is looking for an experienced and highly motivated Inventory Controller to join our Supply Chain team.
 The successful candidate will be responsible for maintaining accurate inventory records, monitoring stock movements, conducting stock reconciliations, investigating inventory discrepancies, and ensuring effective inventory control across warehouse operations. Strong experience with SAP-based inventory management, stock control and Excel will be important for success in this role.


 


 


Key Responsibilities




Conduct physical stock checks and inspections.


Manage damaged-stock reporting and inventory adjustments.


Investigate inventory discrepancies and resolve root causes with Operations.


Reconcile lost-and-found stock, short receipts and over-receipts.


Track and reconcile product recalls and withdrawals.


Troubleshoot inventory issues in 
SAP and TWMS
.


Reverse incorrect SAP/TWMS adjustment and production-inbound entries.


Maintain audit-compliant inventory records and transactional traceability.


Manage damaged and aged finished goods, including batch corrections.


Raise and process disposal stock adjustment documentation.


Maintain stock availability in SAP/TWMS for raw materials, packaging materials and finished goods.


Monitor and clear virtual rack locations in TWMS.




Qualifications & Experience




Minimum bachelor’s degree in business & management.


2+ years inventory/stock-management experience in an SAP-based environment.


Strong Excel, data gathering and analytical skills.


Root-cause analysis and continuous-improvement mindset


Ability to work effectively under operational and time pressures.


Strong time-management skills and ability to work cross-functionally.

Key Competencies




Excellent communication


Time management


Teamwork


Self-motivation


Flexibility and reliability


Attention to detail


Growth mindset


Results focus


Constructive collaboration




Be part of the Skel life and join a team that values healthy eating and active lifestyles and wants to share that with all the people of PNG. Email your EOI and CV/Resume/Supporting Docs in 1 PDF file and send to email: 
[email protected]
.


In the subject line address as 
“Inventory Controller".


Applications close

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

28764.description:
Senior Lecturer


School of Accounting & Finance (SoAF) - Port Moresby, NCD


Position Title: Senior Lecturer
Department: School of Accounting & Finance (SoAF)
Location: IBSUniversity, 11 Mile Campus
Reports To: Head - School of Accounting & Finance


Employment Type: Full-Time


ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT:


The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its’ humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades & Associates primarily providing revision classes for the needs of Papua New Guinea. Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG) has evolved into a private University level Institution over the last 38 years. Today we are one of the largest business schools in the country and off degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies and Information Technology. We also continue to provide study pathways for grade 10 & 12 school leavers including industry accreditations for those seasoned professionals who want to get certified in their field.


Our success is the fruits of our dedicated team committed to making a difference in Papua New Guinea, through their efforts to help educate current and futures citizens on Papua New Guinea.


A CAREER WITH US:


At IBS we believe that everyone has been gifted with natural talents and learnt skills. Our recruitment process is designed to help candidates understand this and enable us to better match you with a role that you will not only be able to do but enjoy doing. Career progression is also important to us and believes that each employee should be at the driving seat of their career progression - this means your manager will discuss with you where you want to be in the future and be more of a coach for you in terms of giving you feedback on areas you need to work on to be your best and achieve your goals. We also have a lot of staff events that enable us to celebrate as a team and give recognition where it's due.


ABOUT THE ROLE


The Lecturer plays a pivotal role to ensure we have highly engaged and productive students that are enriched through education in unison to prosper in their life goals and achievements. As the gatekeeper of our student’s success, you will promote student management best practices that can be easily digested and embraced across the organization.


The Lecturer is responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining a modern Academic function that is digital on the inside—harnessing digital + cloud technologies to effectively capture and manage all aspects of delivering the best student experience for the Institution. Overseeing and managing the entire lecturing process, you will ensure all students are engaged both academically and socially to maintain a healthy balance and effectively utilize our finite academic infrastructure resources. This position incorporates a high degree of unsupervised work; as an outcome focused person, you will display strong conflict resolution skills and enjoy managing your workload and being part of a productive team.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:


In a highly student-focused role, the Lecturer should focus on strong collaboration, communication, negotiation and interpersonal skills. It is also essential that you understand Business and Management best practices and local industry trends. Lecturer duties will involve managing and monitoring undergraduate programs. 29044.description:
WE'RE HIRING | MEETINGS & EVENTS CONCIERGE


Food & Beverage | Crowne Plaza Residences Port Moresby


Crowne Plaza Residences Port Moresby is seeking an accomplished Meetings & Events professional with exceptional stakeholder management skills, strong operational leadership and the confidence to deliver complex, high-profile events.


Our Meetings & Events portfolio extends from executive meetings and diplomatic engagements to major conferences and functions involving up to 800 delegates and guests. Delivering events of this scale requires extensive logistical planning, cross-functional coordination, effective resource management and the ability to navigate multiple stakeholder relationships.


This is a highly visible role requiring someone who can take ownership of the client experience, exercise sound operational judgement and confidently engage with senior executives, government representatives, international delegations and key decision-makers.


As our Meetings & Events Concierge, you will be the central point of coordination between clients, hotel departments and external stakeholders, ensuring seamless execution from initial planning through to successful delivery.


Beyond operational leadership, you will leverage established relationships, identify commercial opportunities and work closely with Sales & Marketing to strengthen our market positioning and grow our Meetings & Events business.


A little taste of your day-to-day




Lead the end-to-end coordination and operational execution of meetings, conferences, corporate functions and major events involving up to 800 participants.


Manage complex event logistics, operational readiness, resource allocation and stakeholder expectations across multiple internal departments and external partners.


Serve as the principal client liaison, confidently engaging with senior executives, VIP guests, official delegations and other high-profile stakeholders.


Coordinate closely with security personnel, protocol teams and event organisers to facilitate the professional management of high-profile engagements.


Demonstrate strong leadership through effective delegation, departmental briefings, proactive problem-solving and a visible, hands-on operational presence.


Anticipate operational challenges, manage competing priorities and implement practical solutions to maintain service excellence and business continuity.


Build and leverage strategic client relationships to identify new business opportunities, strengthen client retention and develop long-term partnerships.


Collaborate with Sales & Marketing on business development initiatives, client presentations, venue inspections and the conversion of prospective business.


Maintain accountability for event execution, stakeholder satisfaction, operational standards and post-event performance reviews.




What we need from you


We are seeking an established hospitality professional who brings maturity, confidence and proven operational capability.




A minimum of 5 years' relevant experience in Meetings & Events, conference management, premium hospitality operations or a comparable environment, including direct responsibility for significant event delivery.


Demonstrated experience managing complex, large-scale events requiring extensive logistical coordination and engagement with multiple stakeholders.


Proven ability to coordinate multidisciplinary teams, delegate effectively and maintain operational oversight under pressure.


Strong stakeholder engagement, relationship management, negotiation and communication skills.


The professional confidence and discretion to engage comfortably with senior corporate clients, government representatives, diplomatic delegations and VIP guests.


Sound commercial acumen, with the ability to identify revenue opportunities, support business development and contribute to strategic account growth.


Excellent organisational skills, attention to detail, operational judgement and a proactive approach to risk management.


Flexibility to work evenings, weekends and public holidays in accordance with operational requirements.




Experience within an internationally branded hotel, premium conference venue or an organisation delivering major corporate and government events will be highly regarded.


This is a role requiring proven experience, operational authority and the confidence to take ownership of complex event environments. Candidates must be able to demonstrate direct involvement in leading significant events and managing demanding stakeholder expectations.


What you can expect from us


At IHG Hotels & Resorts, we give our colleagues room to belong, grow and make a difference.


We offer competitive benefits, international career development opportunities, comprehensive training and access to IHG's global colleague benefits.


This is an opportunity to influence a significant area of our business, develop meaningful professional relationships and represent one of the world's leading international hospitality brands.


IHG is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating an inclusive workplace where different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives are valued.


JOIN OUR TEAM


If you are an experienced events professional ready to take on a role with significant operational responsibility, high-profile stakeholder engagement and commercial influence, we invite you to apply.


Please submit your cover letter, relevant qualifications and updated CV to:


[email protected]


Applications close: 2 November 2026, COB.


As part of your application, please outline the largest or most complex event you have personally coordinated, including the number of participants, your specific responsibilities and the key stakeholders involved.


This vacancy is open to PNG citizens only. IHG is an equal opportunity employer.


Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.


 





            

        
Apply

29043.description:
WE'RE HIRING | HEAD OF FOOD & BEVERAGE


Crowne Plaza Residences Port Moresby | IHG Hotels & Resorts


Are you an accomplished Food & Beverage leader with strong culinary foundations, commercial ambition and the ability to lead a dynamic, high-volume hospitality operation?


Crowne Plaza Residences Port Moresby is seeking an experienced Head of Food & Beverage to lead a diverse and demanding operation spanning restaurant and bar services, culinary production, multiple conference and event venues, private functions and extensive outside catering.


This is far more than a traditional restaurant management role.


Our operation includes a busy restaurant and bar trading from 6:30am to 10:00pm, multiple function spaces hosting corporate and social events, daily outside catering commitments and major events serving 800+ guests.


These activities frequently operate simultaneously, requiring exceptional planning, confident leadership, disciplined delegation and the ability to deliver consistently across several revenue streams.


Reporting directly to the General Manager, you will have overall accountability for the performance of the Food & Beverage department, from the quality of the culinary offering and guest experience to commercial growth, profitability, operational standards and people development.


We are looking for a leader who understands the kitchen as well as the dining room, who can develop capable managers and who is equally comfortable reviewing financial performance, meeting corporate clients or leading the delivery of a major event.


A little taste of your day-to-day


Every day is different, but your responsibilities will include:


Operational Leadership & Guest Experience




Lead the entire Food & Beverage operation, including Port Terrace Restaurant & Bar, culinary production, conferencing, events, private functions, outside catering and stewarding.


Provide visible, hands-on leadership across a demanding operation, ensuring that simultaneous restaurant services, functions and catering commitments are appropriately resourced and professionally delivered.


Establish clear operational structures, management coverage and effective delegation, ensuring the department operates consistently across all trading periods.


Maintain exceptional standards of food, beverage, presentation, service and guest engagement.


Personally support significant guest and client interactions, VIP requirements, service recovery and the delivery of high-profile events.




Culinary Leadership & Development




Provide strong culinary oversight, working closely with the Head Chef to maintain exceptional food quality, menu innovation, consistency, presentation and kitchen performance.


Draw on your practical culinary experience to coach, mentor and develop the Head Chef and emerging kitchen leaders, strengthening their technical capability, management skills and accountability.


Monitor kitchen output, production planning, food costs, menu engineering, food safety and operational efficiency.


Ensure culinary operations can meet the demands of restaurant service, banqueting and large-scale outside catering simultaneously without compromising quality.


Develop effective kitchen leadership and succession plans while maintaining a broader focus on the performance of the entire F&B business.




Commercial Performance & Business Development




Take ownership of departmental revenue, profitability, budgets, forecasting, cost controls and overall financial performance.


Identify opportunities to grow restaurant revenue, conference and event business, catering sales and average guest spend.


Work proactively with Sales & Marketing to develop promotions, attract corporate business, strengthen the events pipeline and maximise conversion opportunities.


Ensure commercial initiatives are supported by operational planning, appropriate pricing, menu development and follow-through.


Analyse performance across individual revenue streams, address underperformance and implement measurable improvement plans.


Maintain effective control over purchasing, inventory, food and beverage costs, labour productivity and departmental expenditure.




Conferences, Events & Outside Catering




Oversee the planning and execution of corporate conferences, private functions, major banquets and large-scale outside catering.


Ensure every event has appropriate staffing, management coverage, equipment, logistical arrangements and operational contingency plans.


Work closely with the Conferences & Events team and Meetings & Events Concierge to coordinate client requirements, event readiness, operational delivery and seamless execution.


Provide visible leadership during significant events, supporting the team with guest engagement, service standards, timing and problem resolution.


Review event profitability, client satisfaction and feedback to improve delivery and encourage repeat business.




People, Standards & Compliance




Lead, coach and develop managers, supervisors, culinary leaders and frontline colleagues, creating a culture of accountability, professionalism and continuous improvement.


Build a capable leadership structure that supports effective delegation, colleague progression and operational continuity.


Maintain compliance with HACCP, food safety, workplace safety, brand standards and operational audit requirements.


Foster a collaborative environment where front of house, back of house, Sales & Marketing and supporting departments work together towards shared commercial and guest experience objectives.




What we need from you


We are seeking a well-rounded hospitality professional who combines strong practical culinary knowledge with proven Food & Beverage leadership and commercial capability.


The successful candidate will demonstrate:




Significant progressive leadership experience within quality hotels, resorts or complex, multi-outlet Food & Beverage operations.


A strong practical culinary background, with the technical confidence to assess kitchen performance, maintain product standards and coach professional kitchen leaders.


Proven experience managing restaurant operations alongside conferences, banqueting, functions and large-scale catering.


The ability to coordinate multiple simultaneous operational commitments while maintaining consistent quality and service.


Demonstrated commercial success, with a sound understanding of budgets, P&L management, forecasting, food costs, menu engineering, inventory control and labour productivity.


Strong people leadership skills, including the ability to mentor managers, develop emerging talent and deliver results through others.


Excellent communication, client engagement and stakeholder management skills.


A proactive approach to business development, guest satisfaction and continuous operational improvement.


Sound knowledge of HACCP, food safety and hospitality compliance requirements.


Relevant culinary or hospitality qualifications, or equivalent professional experience.


The flexibility and commitment required to support a hospitality operation spanning early mornings, evenings, weekends, public holidays and major events.




Above all, we are looking for a leader who takes ownership. Someone who can see the bigger picture, develop the people around them and ensure that every part of the operation contributes to the success of the business.


What you can expect from us


At IHG Hotels & Resorts, we give our people the room to belong, grow and make a difference.


You will join a globally recognised hospitality organisation offering a competitive remuneration package, hotel room discounts, professional development opportunities and access to some of the best training and career development programmes in the industry.


We believe great hospitality starts with great people. Our culture is built on trust, respect, collaboration and a genuine commitment to creating an inclusive workplace where colleagues can thrive.


Through our myWellbeing framework, we also support our colleagues' health, lifestyle and workplace wellbeing.


This is an opportunity to take ownership of a significant hospitality operation, develop its future leaders and contribute directly to the continued growth of Crowne Plaza Residences Port Moresby.


Join us today!


Ready to take the next step in your Food & Beverage leadership career?


Please submit your cover letter, updated CV and relevant qualifications to:


[email protected]


Applications close: 2 November 2026 (close of business)


This vacancy is open to PNG citizens only.


IHG Hotels & Resorts is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace for all colleagues.


Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

SPECTRA LAE IS HIRING!


Purchasing Officer


Spectra Industrial Limited - a Leader in Sales, Service and Hire of Forklifts, Gensets and Industrial Supplies, is seeking organized and well experienced individuals to join our Lae Accounts/Admin Team and be a part of our growing enterprise! 


Position Description




Position Title: 
Purchasing
 Officer


Company: Spectra Industrial


Location: Lae, Papua New Guinea


Reports To: Financial Controller




Position Purpose


The Purchasing Officer is responsible for sourcing goods and materials, obtaining and evaluating quotations, negotiating with suppliers, preparing purchase orders, and coordinating deliveries. The role supports cost control and stock availability through accurate costing, effective procurement, supplier relationship management, and close coordination with inventory and operational teams.


Key Responsibilities




Source goods, materials, and services in accordance with approved specifications, budgets, and purchasing procedures.


Request, compare, and evaluate supplier quotations, including pricing, costing, quality, lead times, and commercial terms.


Negotiate prices, payment terms, delivery schedules, and supply conditions to achieve value for money.


Prepare and process purchase orders accurately and maintain complete procurement records.


Monitor outstanding orders, coordinate deliveries, and follow up suppliers to prevent stock shortages and operational delays.


Complete accurate landed-cost calculations and promptly receipt incoming stock into the inventory management system, ensuring quantities, unit costs, and supporting documentation reconcile with purchase orders and supplier invoices.


Work closely with stores and inventory teams to maintain appropriate stock levels, investigate variances, and support accurate stock and inventory management.




Key Competencies & Skills




Demonstrated costing or inventory experience is strongly required.


Proven procurement experience, including sourcing, quotation analysis, purchase order processing, and supplier follow-up.


Strong supplier negotiation skills and sound commercial judgment.


Practical experience in stock and inventory management, including stock-level monitoring and reconciliation.


Detail-oriented, accurate, and highly organized, with the ability to manage competing priorities.


Strong analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills.


Computer literacy, with proficiency in Microsoft Excel and purchasing or inventory management systems.




Qualifications & Experience




Diploma or Degree in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Business, Accounting, or a related discipline.


Minimum 3–5 years’ experience in purchasing, procurement, supply chain, or a similar commercial role.


Applicants must have hands-on costing or inventory experience, candidates without this background will not meet the essential requirement.


Demonstrated experience in supplier negotiation and stock or inventory management.


Experience with Odoo or a comparable procurement and inventory system will be an advantage.

Malekula Street

28973.description:
Fixed term contract up to November 2027 (with possible extension)


Based in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea


Open to PNG and International candidates




 


About Palladium


Palladium is a global leader in the design, development, and delivery of Positive Impact – the intentional creation of enduring social and economic value.  We work with governments, businesses, and investors to solve the world's most pressing challenges. With a team of more than 2,000 employees operating in 75-plus countries and a global network of over 35,000 experts, we help improve economies, societies, and, most importantly, people's lives.
 


About PNG-Australia Strongim Wok Long TVET (SWLT)


The PNG–Australia Strongim Wok Long Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) (SWLT) program is a four-year, AUD 80 million investment by the Australian Government Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) to support Papua New Guinea’s (PNG) efforts to strengthen its TVET sector. Aligned with PNG’s national priority to build an educated and skilled workforce for resilient economic growth, SWLT aims to enhance the quality, relevance, and inclusiveness of skills development. The program supports improvements in national quality assurance systems, technical college standards, graduate employability, and Australia’s visible and trusted development partnership with PNG.


The program aligns with the broader goals of the 
Australia–PNG Development Partnership Plan 2024–2029
, which emphasises locally led development, education investment, and inclusive growth, as well as 
PNG’s Higher and Technical Education Reform Act 2020
.


This Opportunity


As 
Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Adviser
 you will provide MEL and performance management advisory support to PNG’s Department of Higher Education, Research, Science, and Technology (DHERST) to strengthen its capability to monitor, evaluate, report on and learn from implementation of priority higher education and TVET reforms. You will support improved decision-making, accountability, learning and adaptation by helping DHERST establish practical systems and processes for tracking reform progress, outcomes and longer-term impacts.


About you


You will demonstrate proven experience in the following areas:


MEL and performance systems




Review DHERST’s existing MEL and performance management frameworks, systems, tools, processes, indicators, data sources and reporting requirements.


Support DHERST to develop or refine a practical MEL framework, underpinned by a theory of change or similar logic, to monitor and evaluate reform implementation, outcomes and learning.


Support the development of outcome, output and process indicators aligned with DHERST’s Corporate Plan, reform priorities and reporting commitments.


Identify practical data sources, baselines, targets, collection methods, collection frequency, roles and responsibilities, data storage arrangements, analysis approaches and reporting formats.


Support the development of dashboards, performance reporting systems and other tools that strengthen DHERST’s ability to access, analyse and use performance information.




Reform monitoring, reporting and learning




Support DHERST to monitor, evaluate and report on implementation and outcomes of priority higher education and TVET reforms.


Provide advice and support to improve reporting against GoPNG, DHERST and related sector commitments, including commitments under the Joint Statement of Intent where relevant.


Support DHERST to establish or strengthen regular forums and processes for reviewing progress, identifying emerging trends, discussing risks and opportunities, and adapting implementation approaches.


Contribute to reports, briefs, factsheets, communications products and other knowledge products that use performance information to support evidence-based decision-making.


Support DHERST to identify baseline information and develop practical approaches for tracking progress over time.




Coordination and integration




Work closely with DHERST counterparts, SWLT team members and other related activities to ensure approaches are coherent and complementary, including participation in schedule coordination meeting within SWLT, DHERST and DFAT.


Support alignment between MEL, planning, budgeting, reporting, reform implementation and digital systems development where relevant.


Engage with relevant GoPNG stakeholders, development partners and other sector actors as required to support coherence, avoid duplication and strengthen the use of existing systems and processes.


Ensure proposed MEL approaches are proportionate, contextually appropriate, GEDSI sensitive and responsive, locally led and sustainable.




Capacity 
streng
t
hening




Mentor and support nominated DHERST counterparts to strengthen their capability to lead and manage MEL and performance management functions.


Provide practical coaching, training, orientation and on-the-job support to DHERST staff to operationalise agreed MEL systems, tools and processes.


Support the development of standard operating procedures, templates, guidance notes and other practical resources that enable DHERST staff to sustain MEL functions beyond the assignment.


Participate in self-reflection, feedback and pulse-check activities to monitor the effectiveness of the capability strengthening approach and adjust support in response to feedback.




Cross-cutting priorities




Ensure MEL approaches consider and address a) gender equality, b) disability and c) social inclusion, locally led development, child protection and PSEAH safeguarding, sustainability and other SWLT cross-cutting priorities.


Support the collection and use of disaggregated data where practical and appropriate, including data relevant to gender, disability, youth, location and other priority groups.


Ensure proposed systems, tools and reporting processes are practical, ethical, inclusive and aligned with SWLT and DHERST requirements.




General SWLT 




Contribute to the development and implementation of solutions that deliver value and ensure SWLT principles
[1]
 are embedded within program delivery.


Comply with all safeguarding, child protection and PSEAH requirements, and promptly report any safeguarding concerns in accordance with SWLT and Palladium policies and procedures.

28972.description:
Engineer - Medium Term Planning – Mine Engineering Services Open Pit (242805)


About Us


New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.


NPL now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our Mine Technical Services Department as 
Engineer - Medium Term Planning – Mine Engineering Services Open Pit.


About the role


Reporting to the Senior Engineer – Mine Engineering Services, the Medium-Term Planning Engineer is responsible for developing and maintaining medium-term mine plans that optimize production, safety, operational efficiency, and economic performance. The role bridges long-term strategic planning and short-term operational execution, typically from monthly to 1 year.


The engineer works closely with geology, operations, drill and blast, survey, geotechnical, and processing teams to ensure achievable and practical mine schedules aligned with business objectives.


In this role, you will:




Develop and maintain medium-term mine plans, production schedules, and sequencing strategies.


Generate rolling forecasts for ore and waste movement.


Prepare designs for pit stages, pushbacks, stopes, haul roads, dumps, and stockpiles.


Familiarity with mine planning and scheduling software such as Deswik, Vulcan, MineSched, or similar.


Ensure plans align with life-of-mine strategy and annual budget targets.


Optimize mine extraction sequences to maximize value and operational efficiency.


Conduct mining studies and trade-off evaluations.


Analyze production performance against plan and recommend corrective actions.


Monitor mine productivity, dilution, ore loss, and equipment utilization.


Maintain a high level of health, safety and environmental awareness and comply with all relevant NPL policies & procedures. 




About You


To succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experience.




Tertiary qualifications in Mining Engineering


Typically, 3- 5 years of mining engineering experience.


Experience in open pit and or underground mine planning.


Exposure to medium-term scheduling and operational mine planning.


Experience with production forecasting and mining optimization.


Familiarity with mine planning and scheduling software such as Deswik, Vulcan, MineSched, or similar.


Understanding Life of Mine Planning and experience in sourcing and developing input to same.


Geological modelling, mine planning & scheduling software packages.


Extensive Open Pit Mine Planning experience (short term to medium term)


Good computer skills with the ability to use integrated management systems, word processing, presentation and spreadsheet applications.




Mobilization Requirement 


This is a PNG National position, a site-based role on a FIFO arrangement with a rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off. Candidates must successfully pass a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening (to be arranged only for successful candidates after the interview stage), and provide an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months). Candidates must be PNG Nationals and available to start immediately. Females are encouraged to apply.


Join Our Team as an Engineer- Medium Term Planning – Mine Engineering Services Open Pit


Embark on a rewarding career with New Porgera Limited as an Engineer - Medium Term Planning – Mine Engineering Services Open Pit. This role offers a unique opportunity to work with a dynamic team to contribute to NPL’s success. Enjoy a balanced work schedule, competitive compensation, and a chance to develop your career and technical expertise in a supportive and professional environment.


 


Note:
 This advert will be open until 
02
nd
 November 2026
. If you do not hear from NPL within next two (2) weeks following the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful for this opportunity.





    	        
Apply

28753.description:
About Sarens
Sarens is a global leader in crane rental, heavy lifting, and engineered transport. For over a century, we have built a reputation for solving the lifting and transport challenges others walk away from, and our philosophy is simple: nothing too heavy, nothing too high.


Our people work on some of the world's most demanding projects in mining, oil and gas, energy, infrastructure, and construction. In Oceania, we operate across Australia, Papua New Guinea, and New Caledonia, with the backing of a global organisation that shares engineering expertise, equipment, and knowledge across borders.


We are guided by five values: Brilliant Solutions, Love for Tradition, Dedication to Safety, Global Spirit, and Zeal for Excellence.


About the role
Based in Port Moresby and reporting to the Regional Director, Oceania, you'll lead Sarens in Papua New Guinea. You'll be the senior Sarens representative in the country, responsible for the safety, commercial, and operational performance of the business.


This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll spend time with clients, on project sites, and with your team, not just behind a desk. You'll set the direction for the business in Papua New Guinea, build long-term client relationships, and grow a capable local team that can deliver complex heavy lift and transport work safely. Regular travel to project sites across the country is part of the role.


What you'll do


Safety and compliance




Lead a strong safety culture where every person goes home safe, every day


Ensure all work meets Sarens SHEQ standards, client requirements, and Papua New Guinea legislation


Ensure compliance with Papua New Guinea employment, tax, customs, and regulatory requirements, including work permits and visas


Manage security, logistics, and risk in remote and challenging locations




Commercial and growth




Own the country P&L, including budgeting, forecasting, pricing, and cost control


Identify and win new work, leading tenders and commercial negotiations


Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, contractors, government bodies, and landowner and community stakeholders


Manage contracts, variations, and credit to protect margin and cash flow




Operations




Oversee day-to-day operations, ensuring projects are delivered safely, on time, and to budget


Manage fleet deployment, maintenance, and utilisation, working with the Fleet and Technical Solutions teams


Work with our engineers to plan complex lifts and moves


Drive continuous improvement in efficiency, quality, and client service




People and leadership




Recruit, develop, and retain a capable team, with a strong focus on building Papua New Guinea national talent


Lead training and career development so local employees can grow into senior roles


Maintain positive employee and industrial relations


Work closely with regional HR, Finance, SHEQ, and Fleet functions




Reporting




Report regularly on safety, financial, and operational performance to regional leadership


Contribute to Oceania strategy and annual business planning




What you'll bring




5+ years' senior leadership experience in cranage, heavy lift, transport, mining services, or a related industry


Proven experience running a business unit or operation with P&L responsibility


Strong experience working in Papua New Guinea, with a sound understanding of its business, regulatory, and community environment


A strong track record in safety leadership


Commercial acumen, with experience in tendering, contracts, and client management


The ability to lead and develop culturally diverse teams


Resilience, sound judgement, and a practical approach to problem solving


Clear, confident communication with clients, crews, and senior leaders alike




What success looks like in your first year




A safe year, with a visible and trusted safety culture across all sites


Strong relationships with key clients and a growing pipeline of work


A stable, capable team, with clear development plans for national employees


A business delivering to budget, with sound financial controls in place




What we offer




Competitive Salary package


The backing of a global organisation with deep heavy lift expertise


Real autonomy and the chance to shape the future of the business in Papua New Guinea


Career opportunities across Oceania and the wider Sarens network




Ready to apply?
Click Apply and send us your resume and a cover letter outlining your leadership experience in Papua New Guinea and what you would bring to the role. We strongly encourage applications from Papua New Guinea nationals.


 





    	        
Apply

29067.description:
Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


About the role


This position is responsible for the efficient manufacture of components and assemblies of fabricated metal products for K92’s growing mine site. Work as part of a team and operate machines to produce parts or tools by turning, boring, milling, planning, shaping, slotting, grinding or drilling metal stock or components.


Key Accountabilities




Set up and adjust metalworking machines and equipment. Operate machines to produce parts or tools by turning, boring, milling, planning, shaping, slotting, grinding or drilling metal stock or components.


Fit and assemble metal parts, tools, or sub-assemblies, including welding or brazing parts.


To efficiently manufacture components and assemblies of a project, whilst constantly looking at methods or procedures to reduce cost and time required but not compromising quality.


To complete work to the highest possible standard.

28897.description:
Assistant Mill Manager – Palm Oil Mill


 


An opportunity to lead a safe, efficient and sustainable mill operations


 


About the Role


We are seeking an experienced and capable Assistant Mill Manager to support the Mill Manager in leading day-to-day palm oil mill operations. The position covers the full production process—from receipt of Fresh Fruit Bunches through extraction, storage and dispatch of Crude Palm Oil and Palm Kernel—as well as utilities, maintenance coordination and effluent treatment.


As deputy to the Mill Manager, you will provide hands-on operational leadership, maintain production and quality standards, strengthen safety and environmental performance, and support the development of mill employees.


 


Key Responsibilities




Supervise daily processing to achieve production, Oil Extraction Rate and Kernel Extraction Rate targets while minimising losses.


Monitor process parameters and ensure CPO and Palm Kernel meet required specifications.


Coordinate process, boiler, maintenance, workshop, laboratory, utilities and treatment plant activities.


Support preventive and corrective maintenance and reduce unplanned downtime.


Lead, coach and develop section heads, supervisors and operators.


Promote compliance with safety, environmental, quality and sustainability requirements.


Monitor operational costs, utilities, consumables and stock balances, and recommend improvements.


Act on behalf of the Mill Manager when required.




 


What You Will Bring




Strong practical knowledge of palm oil milling, production control and process optimisation.


Demonstrated ability to supervise multidisciplinary mill operations and coordinate maintenance activities.


Sound leadership, communication, reporting and problem-solving skills.


A strong commitment to safety, environmental compliance, quality and continuous improvement.


Ability to manage priorities, control costs and make sound operational decisions.




 


Academic Requirements




Diploma or degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Chemical/Process or Agricultural Engineering, or another relevant technical discipline.


A bachelor’s degree and training or certification in palm oil milling, boiler operations, environmental management, ISO, RSPO, ISCC or HACCP will be advantageous.


A supervisory or management qualification will be highly regarded.




 


Skills and Experience Requirements




Five to eight years’ palm oil milling experience, including two to three years in supervision.


Practical knowledge of production, process optimisation, utilities, maintenance and quality control.


Proven ability to coordinate mill operations, manage breakdowns and improve equipment reliability.


Strong leadership, coaching, analytical, reporting and decision-making skills.


Working knowledge of HSE, environmental and sustainability requirements.


Ability to deputise for the Mill Manager and use Excel and production reporting systems.




 


Benefits


A competitive salary packages, including housing, utilities and other benefits will be offered for the role and will be discussed during the interview.


 


How to Apply


If you possess the necessary skills and experience for the Sustainability role, please send your expression of interest and CV to  
[email protected]
, NLT 30
th
 October 2026. Please title your email as “Assistant Mill Manager Application”


 


Join Hargy Oil Palms Limited and be part of a forward-thinking team making a difference in the palm oil industry!

About the position


The Driller is responsible for operating surface and underground diamond drill rigs to extract core samples for geological analysis. This role requires strong technical proficiency, adherence to safety standards, and the ability to work in remote and demanding environments. The Driller ensures accurate core recovery, maintains equipment to a high standard, and supports the overall success of drilling operations.


 


Job Title: 
Diamond Driller (Surface) / Diamond Driller (Underground)
Location: 
Field-Based 
Employment Type: 
Full-Time


Additional Benefits: 




Monthly Shared Drill Bonus


Service Incentive


Medical Insurance Coverage, effective upon successful completion of the probationary period. Terms and conditions apply.




 


Diamond Driller (Surface)


 


Key Responsibilities




Conduct surface diamond drilling operations with a strong focus on safety, quality, and efficiency.


Operate surface drill rigs capable of deep‑hole drilling up to 1,500 meters.


Perform grouting activities and ensure all grouting requirements are met.


Operate, maintain, and troubleshoot surface diamond drill rigs and associated equipment.


Ensure accurate core sampling, logging, and reporting, targeting 100% core recovery.


Carry out routine maintenance and minor repairs on drilling rigs and tools.


Comply with all Company and Client Safety Standards, Policies, and Procedures at all times.


Work collaboratively with the project team to meet operational targets and deadlines.


Provide leadership, coaching, and mentoring to junior drillers.


Demonstrate strong communication skills—both written and verbal.


Exhibit personal attributes such as initiative, honesty, reliability, and the ability to effectively prioritize workload.


Hold relevant qualifications and proven drilling experience.




Diamond Driller (Underground)


Key Responsibilities




Conduct underground diamond drilling operations safely, efficiently, and to a high standard of quality.


Operate and maintain underground diamond drill rigs and associated equipment.


Ensure accurate core sampling, logging, and reporting, achieving 100% core recovery.


Troubleshoot issues and perform routine maintenance on drilling rigs and tools.


Strictly adhere to Company and Client Safety Standards, Policies, and Procedures.


Collaborate with the project team to achieve operational goals and timelines.


Provide guidance, leadership, and mentorship to junior drillers.


Adapt to demanding underground working conditions while upholding all safety protocols.


Communicate effectively in both written and verbal forms.


Display strong initiative, honesty, reliability, and effective workload‑management skills.


Possess relevant qualifications and experience in underground diamond drilling.




Requirements




Strong technical understanding of diamond drilling methods, rig operation, and equipment maintenance.


Ability to monitor drilling parameters and adjust techniques to maximize core recovery.


Knowledge of drilling fluids, sampling processes, and mechanical troubleshooting.


Relevant industry certifications and proven operational experience.


Ability to pass a full Pre‑Employment Medical Examination.


Valid Police Clearance Certificate.




Key Personal Attributes




Proven ability to lead, mentor, and develop junior drillers.


Strong verbal and written communication skills.


High level of initiative, honesty, and reliability.


Ability to manage priorities and work effectively under pressure.

Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.


Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.


About the role




Maintain mining equipment tyres and rim assemblies.


Knowledge of machines and tools, including their designs, uses, repair, and maintenance.


Capable of working safe and promote a safe working environment.




Key / Major Accountabilities




Assessment of tyre wear patterns.


Distinguish tyres wearing unevenly and recommend solutions.


Must have knowledge of tire pressure levels and methods to repair and patch damaged tires.


Recommend certain types of tyres based on vehicles and driving patterns also considering the geographical locations and weather conditions.


Locate punctures in tubeless tyres by visual inspection or by immersing inflated tyres in water baths and observing air bubbles.


Remove, fit and inspect wheel alignments.


Conduct NDT rim inspection


Able to remove and install earthmoving tyres with mechanical aids.


Repair tyre machines or systems using the needed tools.


Follow safety procedures and guidelines in place and strict observance of housekeeping.


Identify and report safety hazards.


Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.


Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.




About You 


To be considered for this role, it is essential that you should have;




Grade 10 certificate


3 years’ experience in Heavy Equipment Tyre repairs or Automotive Mechanic.


Sound communication skills             


Self-starter, and very resourceful, with the ability to find solutions to problems to ensure the equipment availability is high.


Flexible and adaptable and be a team player.


Able to work long hours.


Must have valid driving license (Class 3 or above)


Must be able to operate tyre handling machines




Life at K92 


Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.


Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.


We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster. 


If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.


THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP 





    	        
Apply

POSITION 
TERMS OF REFERENCE


 


POSITION TITLE:
 
Deputy Principal, Hon. Roy Biyama Balimo Academy 
2027 Academic year


AREA: 
Balimo, Delta Fly, Western Province


LOCATION: Balimo College Campus


TYPE / DURATION: full-time, 12-month contract, 6-month probationary period


REMUNERATION: Competitive Salary Package


 


Re-advertised – previous applicants need not re-apply


 


ABOUT KTF:


KTF is an Australian international aid and development organisation working in Papua New Guinea (PNG).


 


We work with people and communities to improve the lives and futures of Papua New Guineans. We do this by: assisting remote and rural communities with access to elementary and primary 
education
;
 improving access to quality and accessible 
healthcare
;
 improving 
equality 
and access to sustainable income-generation opportunities, especially for women; and by fostering the next generation of 
leaders
. 


 


KTF is a member of the Australian Council for International Development and is accredited with the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade’s Australian Not-for-Profit Cooperation Program.


 


THE BALIMO COLLEGE EDUCATIONAL CAMPUS: 


The Balimo College educational campus was established by SDP in 2019 to build the education and health standards and pathways for the Western Province. Through the college, SDP delivers tertiary qualifications in Teaching under the Balimo Teachers College program; provides secondary school certification and GPA upgrades through Flexible Open Distance Education (FODE); supports schools in the area through E-Learning programs; and in 2024, opened the Hon. Roy Biyama Balimo Academy.


 


HON. ROY BIYAMA BALIMO ACADEMY (the Academy):


The Academy is a PNG Sustainable Development Program initiative implemented in partnership with KTF. The Academy caters for all levels of schooling, including Early Childhood Education, Primary Schooling and Secondary Schooling, and aims to grow to support 1,000 students by the end of 2028. The Academy fosters an environment conducive to quality teaching and learning, being inclusive and responsive to additional needs, and removing educational barriers for local students to learn and grow in a safe and supportive environment.


 


ABOUT THE ROLE:


The Deputy Principal – Secondary will work closely with the Principal to provide leadership across academic, pastoral and administrative aspects of the secondary school. The role will help create the conditions for high-quality teaching and learning, strong student support, effective school systems, and a culture of professionalism and continuous improvement.


The successful candidate will contribute to the leadership of areas such as behaviour management, student wellbeing, enrolment and student records systems, family liaison, assessment and examination preparation, intervention and support programs and the strengthening of academic policies and practices in keeping with RBBA’s goals and values.


This is a hands-on leadership role. The Deputy Principal will be expected to model excellent teaching practice, mentor staff, support professional development, use data to improve outcomes and help ensure that school systems are well organised, consistent and student-centred.


Proficiency in educational technologies and strong leadership skills are essential, along with maintaining confidentiality and privacy within the school environment.


We encourage experienced as well as emerging leaders to apply.


RESPONSIBILITIES:




Support the Principal in the overall leadership and management of the school, including acting in the role of Principal when required.


Help build and sustain a strong culture of teaching excellence, professionalism, accountability and continuous improvement.


Provide leadership in positive behaviour management, student wellbeing and pastoral care systems, ensuring a safe, inclusive and supportive learning environment.


Support and strengthen teaching and learning practices, including SBC implementation, assessment, moderation, reporting and examination preparation.


Use student data and evidence to monitor performance, inform decision-making and implement targeted intervention and support strategies.


Mentor, coach and support teachers and middle leaders, contributing to staff induction, professional learning and performance development.


Maintain a teaching load and model high-quality classroom practice.


Support the effective operation of school systems, including enrolment processes, attendance, student records, reporting and data management.


Lead and support administrative processes to ensure efficient and consistent school operations, with clear systems and accurate record keeping.


Provide support and coordination for boarding operations, working with designated boarding staff to ensure student wellbeing, appropriate supervision and alignment with school policies.


Contribute to the development, implementation and review of school policies and procedures in alignment with organisational and regulatory requirements.


Ensure compliance with key policies including child safeguarding, inclusion, gender equity and organisational codes of conduct.


Support school improvement planning, review processes and the ongoing strengthening of whole-school systems and practices.


Contribute to the management of school resources and budget oversight to support effective and sustainable operations.


Build and maintain strong relationships with students, staff, families and the wider community, supporting positive engagement and communication.


Work collaboratively with partner organisations and stakeholders to support the effective operation and development of the school.


Support and coordinate targeted academic, behavioural and wellbeing programs for students requiring additional support.


Undertake additional duties as directed by the Principal.




SKILLS, ATTRIBUTES & SELECTION CRITERIA:


The successful applicant will demonstrate:


Leadership & Professional Practice




Proven experience in educational leadership, preferably in a secondary or comparable school setting.


Demonstrated ability to lead, motivate and inspire staff, and contribute effectively as part of a leadership team.


Strong professional judgement, integrity, resilience and the ability to remain calm, adaptable and solutions-focused in a complex environment.




Teaching & Learning Expertise




Strong instructional leadership with the ability to support high-quality teaching and learning.


Experience in curriculum implementation, assessment, moderation and examination processes.


Demonstrated ability to use student data and evidence to improve learning outcomes.




Staff Development & Capacity Building




Experience in mentoring, coaching and developing teachers and supporting professional growth.


Ability to build a culture of continuous improvement, collaboration and accountability.




Student Wellbeing & Pastoral Care




Strong experience in behaviour management, pastoral care and student support systems.


Commitment to creating safe, inclusive and supportive learning environments for all students.




Operations & Systems




High-level organisational and administrative skills, including experience with student information systems, records, reporting and school operations.


Ability to develop, implement and maintain effective systems, processes and policies.




Policy, Compliance & Governance




Strong understanding of policy implementation, compliance and regulatory requirements.


Demonstrated commitment to child safeguarding, inclusion and ethical practice.




Community & Stakeholder Engagement




Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build strong relationships with students, staff, families and community stakeholders.


Experience working effectively across cultures and within diverse communities.




Strategic & Operational Capability




Ability to contribute to school improvement planning and strategic development.


Sound understanding of resource management and financial oversight in a school context.




Personal Attributes




High levels of professionalism, initiative and accountability.


Flexibility, adaptability and a proactive approach to problem-solving.


Positive demeanour, strong teamwork skills and an appropriate sense of humour.




Digital & Administrative Capability




Competence in the use of digital tools and systems for communication, data management and school administration.




Qualifications and Experience




A relevant university degree in education or a related field.


A Master’s degree is a pre-requisite.


Current teacher registration, or eligibility for registration, as required.


Substantial teaching experience across a range of school settings.


A strong track record of effective school leadership and improving student outcomes.


Experience in secondary curriculum, assessment and school operations will be highly regarded.

Our client, a major Papua New Guinea organisation, is looking for an experienced Litigation Lawyer to join its in-house Legal team in Port Moresby.

Represent the organisation in negotiations, mediation and other dispute resolution

Manage investigations and evidence gathering
 
Track changes in legislation and case law that affect the organisation

Bachelor of Laws (LLB)
 
Admission as a legal practitioner, with a current practising certificate
 
At least 10 years’ post-admission litigation experience, ideally in a large corporate, resources, energy or government setting

Coordinate with Fleet Administration, Workshop, HR, HSE and project teams.






Perform other duties consistent with the role as directed by management.
